title: The normalized-volume gap in dimension four
main_claim: Every singular boundary-zero klt fourfold germ has normalized volume at most 162, with equality iff it is analytically an ordinary double point. Proof route: assuming nvol >= 162, pass to an isolated Gorenstein K-semistable cone C. Bound stabilizers via transverse-jet valuations, which gives A_C(F) >= 3. Use Hilbert-series/Poisson-summation Fourier tests to force functions of weight below 5/3, then use lc-center subadjunction to get lct_o(m_o) > 3/2. Together these make a general hyperplane section a terminal Gorenstein threefold, so it is cDV and edim(C) <= 5. The germ is then a hypersurface, and Liu's lci theorem applies.

issues.location: Sec. 2, item (iii) and Prop 2.2 (nonisolated case); proof of Thm 1.1
issues.description: The proof relies on external theorems used as black boxes: Liu's lci ODP theorem (Thm 2.12) and the nonisolated bound 4096/27 (Cor 2.18). Their hypotheses as stated (klt, boundary zero, dimension 4) match how the paper uses them. I did not re-verify them.
issues.evidence: 4096/27 = 16*4^4/27 matches nvol(3-fold ODP x A^1), so the bound is plausible. In Prop 2.2 it is used only to exclude a positive-dimensional singular locus on the cone C.

issues.description: The affine (local) subadjunction result, that a minimal lc center is of klt type, is cited from an unpublished internal author-preprint version. The statement is standard in the local setting. Since Z is a G_m-invariant cone, normality and the Cohen-Macaulay property at o spread to all of Z, so the local statement is enough.
issues.evidence: Bibliography: 'Affine Theorem 7.2 is cited from the author preprint, internal version 1.17'.

coverage: I read the full LaTeX proof and checked every step of the main argument. Lemma 2.1 (edim comparison via Izumi): OK. Prop 2.2: index-one cover with dV<=256 forces d=1; graded Nakayama gives a free canonical module. Lemma 3.1 extraction: A_C(v)=A_{C~}(v)+(r-1)v(E) with E reduced on the cover; faithfulness of the slice action. Lemma 3.3: jet count (each character class has density 1/m because the cyclic weights generate Z/m) and the crossing integral, which I verified equals h z0^3. Prop 3.4: Q=mhr^3 >= (2/5)*162=324/5>64, so the delta-derivative 12-3Q^(1/3)<0 and kappa<1 is uniform; A_C(F) >= r ord_F(E) >= r/m > 5/2, and integrality gives >=3. Lemma 4.1: Koszul argument excluding poles; d divides m, so pole frequencies have |t|>=1/(lambda d)>1; Stanley duality sign and grading checked on a weighted polynomial ring; expansion difference of (1-z)^-l checked; Euler-Maclaurin polar part. Lemma 4.2: B(omega)=-L1, B(omega^[q])=(1-2q)L1, and the image shift gives L1>=eL/2q. Prop 4.3: oddness of the measure after the shift x=y+p; a>=432/625; c>=-1 from the x|g2|^2 test; sign analysis of x(l^2-x^2)|g|^2 at every atom; sympy-exact M0..M6=13/16, 61/64, 685/256, 11101/1024 (confirmed directly from the derivatives of the profile); l^2M2-M4=50065/9216; 26581/4096; the closed form of g_3 checked numerically; g(p)=1088sqrt2/(1155pi); RHS about 3.12 < 625/144 < LHS about 4.486. Dimension-3 polynomial integral = 13c/36+65u/216+193/1296 >= 19/324. Dimension-2 integral = 5/27+c/3. The g1 test gives c-u^2/4+1/4 >= 0. Prop 5.1: lct(b^{d0/B}) <= lct(m_o); homogeneity of G; the vertex is not an lc center since r-td0/lambda>0 iff td0<5/2; lc centers lie in V(f_i); the curve, surface and threefold cases, including the residue/adjunction weight bookkeeping (lowers weight by 5q/2-b>0) and the reflexive extension. Prop 6.1: adjunction coefficients A_i-1-b_i>=1 in both cases b_i=1 and b_i>=2, giving terminality, then Reid gives cDV and edim<=5. Final hypersurface/UFD step. I did not independently verify the cited external theorems (Liu, Fujino-Gongyo, Xu-Zhuang, Li-Xu).
